full_judgment: 12. Mr Abdul Malek submits that there are glaring inconsistencies and contradictions in the evidence of PWs 2, 3 and 4, as to the manner of stabbing the deceased. Moreover, their evidence is not consistent with the medical evidence. So there is serious doubt as to their witnessing the occurrence. Hiran, in front of whose shop the occurrence allegedly took place, was a vital witness. But the prosecution without any explanation withheld him. For his non-examination, presumption would be that had he been examined he would not have supported the prosecution case. Moreover, witnessing the occurrence by PW 4, who was inside his shop at the relevant time, is very much doubtful. Staying inside the shop it was impracticable for him to witness the occurrence took place in front of the shop of Hiran. The place of occurrence was shifted by PW 2, who said that the occurrence took place in front of his shop. The place of occurrence shown in the sketch map by the letter 'kha' is in front of the shop of Hiran, not in front of his shop shown by the letter 'gha'. The shop of Sentu shown by letter 'chha' in the sketch map is situated to the opposite of the shop of Hiran to the other side of the road. The shop of PW 2 is not to the opposite of the shop of Hiran. So evidence of PW 2 that occurrence took place in front of his shop makes his evidence as an eye-witness incredible. Thus according to Mr Abdul Malek, the prosecution could not prove the charge beyond all reasonable doubt against accused Ripan. So as benefit of doubt he is entitled to get acquittal. Mr Malek, lastly submits that if conviction of Ripan is found correct, in consideration of his tender age the sentence of death awarded to him should be commuted for ends of justice. With these words he prays for rejection of the reference.
